title: Testing Connected Components
description: Learn how to test React components connected to Redux, including mocking the store and testing user interactions.

data.text: Components are the visible part of your application. They read data from Redux and dispatch actions in response to user interactions. Testing these components requires setting up a Redux store, providing it to your component, and verifying that the rendered output matches expectations.
This lesson covers testing connected React components using React Testing Library, which encourages testing components the way users interact with them rather than testing implementation details.

Every test that involves connected components needs a Redux store. Create a helper function that sets up a store with the slices your component needs. This ensures tests are isolated and reproducible.

data.text: With the test utilities in place, you can now render connected components and test their behavior. The key is to set up initial state, render the component, interact with it, and verify the results.

data.text: Components respond to user actions like clicks, form submissions, and keyboard input. Use `@testing-library/user-event` to simulate realistic user behavior rather than firing synthetic events.

data.text: Sometimes you want to test selectors in isolation. While you can test them through component rendering, testing them directly gives you more precise verification of the selector logic.

data.title: Test a Shopping Cart Component
data.description: Write comprehensive tests for a shopping cart component that displays items, totals, and allows quantity updates.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use renderWithProviders to wrap components with Provider
Set up realistic initial state for each test scenario
Use semantic queries like getByRole instead of class names
Prefer userEvent over fireEvent for realistic interactions
Test user interactions by verifying dispatched actions
Test all states: loading, error, empty, and populated
data.takeaway: Component tests with React Testing Library ensure your UI works correctly from the user's perspective while integrating properly with Redux.
